I didn't commit January because the file has a broken row, and the check script never looked at it.

**The broken row:** `R2601-032,C117,399.31,wholesale` (line 33) has no date, so it has 4 fields where the header has 5.

**Why the check said OK:** `scripts/check.sh` only checks files for the year set in `scripts/check.conf`, which is still `year=2025`. So it skipped `data/2026-01.csv` completely. I found the bad row by reading the file myself.

I removed my copy from `data/`, so the repo is as it was and `inbox/2026-01.csv` is untouched.

**To go ahead:**
1. Fix the source row by adding the missing date. I can't work out what it should be.
2. Decide how the check should handle 2026. You could set `check.conf` to `year=2026`, but then it stops checking 2025 files. Or I could change `check.sh` to check every `data/*.csv`. I haven't changed either because it alters a shared check; tell me which you want.

Once both are done I'll re-run the check and commit as `2026-01: add rows`.

**Also:** row `R2512-003` in December, which I committed last time, has the category `wholsale` instead of `wholesale`. The check only counts fields, so it passed. I haven't changed it; tell me if you want it fixed.
